result.title: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
result.summary: Facial deepfake detectors are usually trained on blending fakes, where a generated face is pasted back into a real frame. Recent generators synthesize the entire face and leave no traces of blending. On a benchmark of 19 datasets released from 2019 to 2026, the best prior facial deepfake detector reaches a mean AUROC of 96.2% on ten blending datasets, but none exceeds 78.1% on five datasets of entire face synthesis (EFS). AI-generated content (AIGC) detectors do not close this gap. We propose TwinD, a detector trained on FaceForensics++ fakes and two kinds of twins: fakes made from a real frame. A reconstruction twin is a real frame reconstructed by an autoencoder, with the real pixels put back in a random region. It targets the neural traces of a decoder. A blob twin blends an altered copy of a real frame with the frame itself, targeting blending artifacts. It needs no generator and no face-shaped mask. Together, these twins provide two complementary forensic cues that generalize to unseen manipulations. TwinDreaches a mean AUROC of 96.3%, 8.9 points above the prior state-of-the-art, with 98.1% on the blending datasets and 95.6% on the EFS datasets. Trained on twins alone, without a deepfake dataset, single models still reach 94.3% on average over three seeds. For reproducibility, the code, trained model, and training data are at: https://github.com/yermandy/TwinD

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出现有面部 deepfake 检测器在整脸合成（EFS）数据上泛化严重不足，提出 TwinD：仅用 FaceForensics++ 假样本与两类「孪生」样本（自编码器重建后回填真实像素、以及真实帧与其篡改副本混合）训练，以捕捉解码器痕迹与混合痕迹，在 19 个数据集上取得明显提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作不涉及 latent 推理，但「用重建残差与合成痕迹判断视觉内容真伪」可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与可靠性判定提供线索，可供核查其线索是否可作为推理前的证据过滤信号。
